This confirms the requested fixes for F1–F4 from my [COMMENTED FIX review](https://github.com/Bimbi-Dev/andes-hackathon/pull/52#pullrequestreview-5560327744). I read the full [author reply](https://github.com/Bimbi-Dev/andes-hackathon/pull/52#issuecomment-6242088598), reviewed the exact `cc4dc5d2dcb1354e4a223fc02946ae7c42f1c961 → b34ca56a79515104d7412d46f0e20d7045a5ba8e` delta, and tested a fresh immutable archive. All 54 archived tracked files still match tree `065cc30d8ce069b8908fc0f763271984049a857c`. The original base remains `bc8eeabfe5220e66a83be972b480a1d1ae8d87d2`; the old candidate remains its unchanged parent.

| Finding | Independent confirmation on this SHA |
| --- | --- |
| F1 — cancellation during request delivery | Revalidation after sink delivery and passive-query setup prevents native GPS acquisition. Unchanged reproduction now reports `nativeCalls:0,timersAfterStop:0`. Uncancelled GPS positive controls remain useful. |
| F2 — motion permission after expiry | Request/session elapsed limits and visibility are checked before the answer and again after permission-event delivery. Unchanged late-grant reproduction now returns `ok:false,listeners:0`. The author suite covers inclusive request/session boundaries, delayed timers, sink-induced changes and grants just inside the limits; the independent positive motion control passes. |
| F3 — conflicting passive grant after denial | Denied/revoked state and original provenance remain terminal within the session; later conflicting evidence is retained without application. Unchanged reproduction now reports `permission:'denied',retry:false`. New-session acquisition and ordinary permission changes still pass. |
| F4 — failure provenance after eviction | GPS errors, local timeouts and platform failures carry original request ID, watch flag and options. The one-event-buffer reproduction now retains `{enableHighAccuracy:false,maximumAge:12345,timeout:23456}`. Success/error positive controls, detached copies and error-message redaction pass. |

Reviewed head `b34ca56`. The code is careful and well tested for what it targets, but as shipped it cannot share location for a whole trip, and its silent stop would cause false alarms with the server-side security check we are adding (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-security-checks-incident-data-design.md`).

**Findings** (`src/phone-observations/adapter.mjs`)
1. **Critical — `:117-127`, `:93`, `:247`:** `finish()` emits nothing to the sink when it stops on the event budget, session timer, `pagehide` or `freeze`. With the defaults (`:6-11`, `maxEvents:256`, `maxSessionMs:300000`) a 1 Hz watch stopped after ~254 s in a probe, and the last event was an ordinary fix. The server only sees silence. The largest allowed budget (`:453-454`) still stops at 60 min.
2. **Critical — `:191`, `:202`, `:248-255`:** every acquisition requires a fresh user activation; a hidden page or screen lock ends the session permanently. There is no Wake Lock and no resume path. Safari < 16.4 has no `userActivation`, so it is always blocked.
3. **Important — `:277`:** `enableHighAccuracy:false` is hard-coded; on Android this means network location, which can be kilometres off on mountain highways.
4. **Important — `:170-176`, `:302-311`:** acquisition returns `unqualified` with `coordinates:null` by default; an integrator must invent a `qualification`, matching `contextKey` and `preciseConsent` to get coordinates.
5. Minor — `:345`: motion only works where `DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission` exists (iOS), never on Android.
6. Minor — `:319`: error events bypass the 1 s throttle and consume `maxEvents`.

**Mapping to the backend** (`POST /v1/trips/:id/locations`, all four fields required, extra fields rejected, one bad item rejects the batch):
```js
e => e.type==='geolocation' && e.data.coordinates?.latitude!=null && e.data.coordinates?.longitude!=null && e.data.accuracyM!=null && e.data.accuracyM<=100000
  ? { capturedAt: new Date(e.sourceTime.value ?? e.clientReceiptTime.wallMs).toISOString(),
      latitude: e.data.coordinates.latitude, longitude: e.data.coordinates.longitude, accuracy: e.data.accuracyM } : null
```
The adapter has no transport: the host must batch 1–100 fixes and reuse one `Idempotency-Key` (visible ASCII, ≤128 chars) per retried batch. Filter out `capturedAt` more than 30 s ahead or 24 h old.

**Minimum to use it in the demo:** emit a stop event from `finish()` (the backend will accept `POST /v1/trips/:id/sharing {state:'stopped'}`), `enableHighAccuracy:true`, raise `maxEvents`/`maxCallbacksPerStream`/`maxSessionMs` to their maximums, add a Wake Lock and a "Reanudar" button. A ~30-line `watchPosition` + Wake Lock + batched POST would also meet the demo need.

Tests: `node --test tests/phone-observations/adapter.test.mjs tests/phone-capability/recorder.test.mjs` → **67 passed** (Node 26.8.1). Findings 1 and 4 reproduced with a probe.

_Review prepared with Claude Code (AI-assisted, read-only verification in a scratch worktree) and posted by @Robertzu43._

> Written by Robert's review agent (Claude), posted from @Robertzu43 at Robert's direction. Reviewed head: `b34ca56`.

**Verdict: request changes.**

**Utility:** The demo needs the phone's GPS sent to `POST /v1/trips/:id/locations` on the backend. This adapter only emits local events and never uploads, so as it stands it doesn't serve the demo. No rule consumes motion data, and PLAN #19 says motion cannot establish a crash, an assault or sleep. **Recommendation: remove motion from this PR and add the upload sink.** Removing motion eliminates blocker 1 and part of blockers 2 and 3, about half the surface.

### Blockers (reproduced by the review probe on `b34ca56`; the suite passes 36/36)

1. **`src/phone-observations/adapter.mjs:213`** The callback budget is counted before rate limiting. At 60 Hz `devicemotion`, the stream shuts itself off after about 17 s (1024 callbacks). The probe got 18 motion events in 30 s, then 0 listeners, inside a 300 s session.
2. **`:319`** `geolocation-error` events skip `minEmitIntervalMs`. Repeated code 2/3 errors (tunnel, yard, the 10 s watch timeout) exhaust `maxEvents` (250) and end the whole session, including active motion. Probe: `stopReason 'event-budget'`.
3. **`:194`** Every `acquisition-blocked` event counts against the shared event budget. A UI that calls `acquireLocation()` on each poll ends the session after 300 blocked calls.
4. **`:417` (privacy)** `revokeConsent()` leaves precise `latitude`/`longitude` in `s.events`, and `snapshot()` keeps returning them until the next `start()`. Purge buffered coordinates on revoke and add a test for it.
5. **`:29`** The synthetic-mode guard only rejects `platform === globalThis`. Passing `Object.create(window)` with a `synthetic-fixture` qualification acquires real GPS and motion with the real clock (confirmed by the probe).

### Should fix

- **`:117`** `finish()` emits no terminal event. A duration timer, pagehide, freeze, budget exhaustion or `stop()` from the sink ends the session without the sink ever being told.
- **`:318`** Code 1 is always treated as a terminal `denied`. Chrome also returns code 1 when the prompt is dismissed, which leaves geolocation blocked for the rest of the session.
- **`:323` / `:373`** The local timeouts start before the user answers the permission prompt. A grant that takes longer than 10 s is discarded, and each retry burns one of the 8 requests.
- **`:216`** The GPS stop event uses `stream: 'geo'`, while every other event uses `'geolocation'`.
- **`:336`** `acquireLocation` returns `{ok:true}` after a synchronous denial or stop.
- **`:152`** The rejection handler in `observePermission` sits on the same `.then`, so a throw in the fulfil path becomes an unhandled rejection.
- **`:373`** A `setTimeout` throw escapes synchronously and leaves `s.motion` stuck on the token.
- **`:354`** Wrong reason codes: sink cancellation returns `session-stopped`, and a backwards clock returns `acquisition-timeout`.
- **`:280` (root cause of F1/F2)** `emit()` calls the untrusted sink in the middle of a state change. Queue the events and flush them once state has settled, instead of adding liveness rechecks at every re-entry point.
- **`:72`** Each event is JSON-serialised three times.
- **`docs/phone-observations/verification.md`, `review-fixes.md`** contain personal local paths (`/Users/sebasbimbi/…`, `/private/tmp/…`) that others can't use to reproduce the runs.

Independent Q52 review: **FIX `4aca76c34a5c1639dccad9cff6a01f00f7023ac2`**. No author source changes or merge.

Read all live PR issue comments (2), formal reviews (4), inline comments/threads (0), plus related #9/#18/#19/#21 issue comments (all0). Both Robert CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews count, including [the newer review5560599386](https://github.com/Bimbi-Dev/andes-hackathon/pull/52#pullrequestreview-5560599386). The six-item disposition does not answer that whole review; passing controls cannot override it.

Six reproducible finding groups remain:

1. **P1 — withdrawal while suspended still permits precise resume** (`adapter.mjs:544–551`, `trip-sharing.mjs:35–37`). Start the trip factory with consent, receive a fix, hide the page, call `revokeConsent()`, show it, then `resumeSharing()`. Actual `{ok:true,calls:2,newPrecise:1}`. Revocation returns early for the inactive adapter, leaving its old consent/intents usable; factory resume does not recheck its cleared consent. Require withdrawal to invalidate stopped-session intents and prevent resumed acquisition. The paired valid-consent resume succeeds and stale callbacks remain inert.
2. **P1 — buffered precise coordinates survive withdrawal**, both active and after stop (Robert blocker4). `snapshot().events` still contains the precise fix. Purge the adapter-owned buffer and retained consent/intents across both states.
3. **P2 — synthetic global alias bypass** (`adapter.mjs:29`, Robert blocker5). `Object.create(globalThis)` with a synthetic qualification and default clock is accepted and calls inherited GPS. Reproduced using inert fake Node globals only:1 native spy call, no real sensor. Direct identity comparison does not enforce the synthetic boundary.
4. **P2 — blocked diagnostic emissions can stop useful GPS** (`:220`, Robert blocker3). With the valid configured ordinary cap10, repeated unqualified motion requests exhaust that shared cap and retire the active GPS watch. The larger default moves the threshold; this is not a claim that the old300-call default symptom persists. Coalesce/throttle rejected diagnostics or obtain an explicit disposition for the retained behavior.
5. **P2 — platform faults escape attribution**: motion `setTimeout` throws synchronously at`:409`; a permission-monitor fulfilment throw becomes an unhandled rejection at`:178–193`. Both should-fix items reproduce; retire tokens and return bounded attributed failures across these paths.
6. **P2 — synchronous GPS denial returns `ok:true`** at`:370` despite permission denied and acquisition already retired. Recheck the settled request outcome before returning success.

[Immutable reviewer report, complete human-feedback disposition, portable commands, probes and actual/expected results](https://github.com/Bimbi-Dev/andes-hackathon/blob/534dba01b2d53bfd970c858be8f2cc53458439dd/review-probes/phone-4aca76c-review.md), reviewer commit `534dba01b2d53bfd970c858be8f2cc53458439dd`, branch `sebasbimbi/test/andes-phone-review-4aca76c`. Reproduce against a disposable exact author archive using the two `ANDES_CANDIDATE_DIR` commands in that report. Only reviewer evidence was added; all57 author archive blobs still match the exact tree.

Independent Node22.22.3 results: author/recorder **82/82 pass**; unchanged original reviewer suite **19/22**, with its three historical expectations superseded by Robert's high-accuracy/browser-managed-motion requests. The original reproduction still passes F1–F3 and differs on F4 only by that accuracy boolean. A separately versioned contract update changes those three expectations explicitly and passes **22/22**; original files/hashes/failures remain untouched. New lifecycle/privacy/fault controls: **8 pass /8 fail**, exit1, grouped above. Positive controls pass for reserved stop slot, nonrecursive reentrant terminal delivery, valid-consent resume and stale callbacks, transient-error throttle/useful fix, default60Hz motion for30 simulated seconds, late/deadline wake-lock release and synchronous legacy gesture scope.

The report also records every remaining should-fix/scope request: code1 prompt dismissal, pre-answer request timeout, stop stream naming, reason codes, ordinary sink transition delivery, serialization, portable author docs, and upload/remove-motion disposition. Actual app Reanudar binding and server sharing receipt remain separate pending integrations; no route is invented. Robert's confirmation is required for his requests. Physical matrix, battery/data, device qualification, locked-screen capture and provider/human evidence remain not-run. Prior scoped acceptance is historical; this exact head is held for correction and re-review.
